privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Chatsoon is a networking app for events, published by Moshi Concepts Inc. ("we", "us"). This policy explains what we collect when you use the Chatsoon apps for iOS and Android and the website at chatsoon.app, why we collect it, who processes it for us and the choices you have. The short version: we collect only what Chatsoon needs to work, we don't show ads, we don't track you across other apps or websites, and we never sell your data.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: Chatsoon is operated by Moshi Concepts Inc., which is responsible for the personal information described in this policy. If you have a question about this policy or your data, email hello@chatsoon.app.

sections.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: We collect only what Chatsoon needs to work. We don't access your phone's address book or your location, and we only receive the photos you choose to take or upload.
bullets: Account: your email address. We use it to send you one-time sign-in codes, to identify your account and to let you know when someone sends you their details with the Connect form. Chatsoon doesn't use passwords.

Your public profile: the name, photo, headline, company, role and links (X, Telegram, Discord, LinkedIn, website, YouTube) you choose to publish, and, if you add them, your mobile number, WhatsApp and Signal details and who can see them, and whether you want it shown in search engines.
Your contacts: the people you add and what you record about them, such as their name, company, role, email, phone, social handles, notes, tags, priority and the event where you met.
Card and badge photos: photos you take of business cards or event badges so Chatsoon can read the details for you.
Connections: when you connect with another Chatsoon user by scanning their QR code, we record that you are connected and, if you set one, the event where you met.

Connect form submissions: when someone sends you their details from your public profile page, we store the name, email address and note they entered, and email you to say they connected. If they tick the tips emails checkbox, we also store that choice and when they agreed to it.

Reports and blocks: if you report or block someone, we store the block, or the report (who or what it's about, the reason and any details you add, and for a reported Connect form message, a copy of that message), and send the report to our moderation inbox for review.
Technical logs: basic information our servers record when the app or website makes a request, such as IP address, device and browser type, and the time and result of the request.

sections.heading: Signing in and connecting accounts with Google, Apple, LinkedIn, X or Discord
paragraphs: If you choose to sign in, create your account, or connect a further account afterwards from Me > Connected accounts, with Google, Apple, LinkedIn, X or Discord, that service shares your name, email address and profile photo with us, and for Discord also your username, so we can create or sign in to your account, prefill your profile, or link the account to the one you're signed in to. X doesn't share an email address with us. We don't receive your password for that service.
bullets: We don't post anything on your behalf, and we don't read your contacts or messages on that service.
You can disconnect Chatsoon from that service any time in its own account settings.
If you use Apple's "Hide My Email", the private address it gives us still works for signing in and for anything we email you.

For Discord, we also record whether two-factor authentication was turned on when you connected it. For X, we record its verification status and follower count at the time you connected it. We use this only to help confirm the account belongs to a real person.

sections.heading: How we use your information
bullets: To sign you in and keep your account secure.
To show your public profile to the people you share it with and, if you turn on search visibility, to search engines.
To store your contacts, notes and tags and keep them in sync across your devices.
To read the details from card and badge photos when you use card scanning.
To deliver connections and connect form submissions to you.
To review reports, enforce our Terms of Use and protect people from spam and abuse.
To run, maintain, secure and fix the service.

sections.heading: No ads, no tracking, no selling
paragraphs: We don't use your information for advertising, we don't build advertising profiles, and we don't track you across other companies' apps or websites. We don't sell or rent your personal information to anyone. If you accept analytics cookies on our website, Google Analytics measures how chatsoon.app is used (see Analytics cookies below); we have Google's advertising features switched off, and it isn't used for advertising.

sections.heading: Analytics cookies
paragraphs: Analytics cookies: with your permission, chatsoon.app uses Google Analytics to understand how the website and web app are used, for example which pages are visited and how people found us. Google Analytics sets cookies and collects information such as pages viewed, the device and browser, approximate location based on IP address, and how you arrived. It is only turned on if you choose Accept in the cookie banner; if you choose Decline or make no choice, it isn't loaded at all. You can change your choice any time with Cookie settings at the bottom of any page or in the Me tab. Google processes this data under its own privacy policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy). The Chatsoon iPhone and Android apps don't use Google Analytics.

sections.heading: Your public profile
paragraphs: Your public profile is public. Anyone who scans your QR code or has your link, which looks like chatsoon.app/id/alex-rivera-7f3a, can see it and save it as a contact card. It shows only what you add to your profile: your name, photo, headline, role, company and links.
Your email address is never shown on your public profile.

Your contacts, notes, tags and priorities are private to you. If you add a mobile number, WhatsApp or Signal, you choose who can see them: people you connect with (Chatsoon users you connect with, and people who send you their details with the Connect form on your page), or anyone with your link. They're never included in the page we give search engines, in our sitemap or in link previews. Tapping WhatsApp or Signal opens that app; Chatsoon doesn't send your details to WhatsApp or Signal.

Search engines: your public profile isn't shown in search engines unless you turn on Show my profile in search engines in Edit profile. When it's on, search engines such as Google and Bing, and AI search services that follow the same rules, can show your name, photo, headline, role, company and links, and we list your profile in our sitemap. We ask AI companies' training crawlers not to collect public profiles. When you turn it off or delete your account, we tell search engines to drop your profile and take it out of our sitemap straight away. Most search engines drop it within a few weeks, but we can't control copies they or other sites have already made.

People you connect with see your public profile and, if you added them, your phone and messaging details. If you let anyone with your link see them, blocking someone doesn't hide them from that person when they're signed out.

Booking links you add (such as Calendly or Google Calendar) are shown on your public profile. When someone books, they do it on that service's page, under its own terms and privacy policy. Chatsoon doesn't see or store the booking.

When you share your profile link in apps such as LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Slack, X or iMessage, the app shows a link preview made from your public profile: an image with your name, photo, role, company and headline, and the same details as text. Your phone, WhatsApp and Signal details are never included in link previews. When you change your profile, new previews show the change, but apps that already made a preview may keep showing their copy for a while, and we can't remove copies they've made.

sections.heading: Connecting with people
paragraphs: When two Chatsoon users connect by scanning a QR code in the app, each of them receives the other's public profile, including their mobile number if they added one, as a contact. That copy stays in their contacts if you later change or remove your number.

When you fill in the Connect form on someone's public profile page, the name, email address and note you enter are sent to that profile's owner and saved in their contacts. Only share details you're happy for them to have. Once they have your details, the profile owner is responsible for how they use them. The form is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, which checks that a person, not a bot, is sending it. The form also has an optional box to email you tips for setting up your own free Chatsoon profile; see Emails we send below.

sections.heading: Emails we send
paragraphs: Account emails: sign-in codes, notices when someone connects with you, and account deletion notices. These are part of the service and can't be turned off while you have an account.

Tips for people who connect with you: if you tick "Email me tips to set up my own free Chatsoon profile" on a Connect form, we send up to three emails over about a week about creating a free profile, and stop when you sign up or unsubscribe. We keep a record of when you agreed and the wording you agreed to.

Tips for account holders: after you sign up, we may send up to two emails with tips for finishing your profile and sharing your link. Turn them off in Me › Tips emails or with the unsubscribe link in any tips email.
Every tips email has an unsubscribe link and identifies us, and we never include other people's messages in them.

sections.heading: Card scanning
paragraphs: When you photograph a business card or badge, the photo is stored privately in your account and sent to Anthropic's Claude AI model, which reads the text and returns the details for you to review. Anthropic processes the photo on our behalf only to provide this service. Under Anthropic's commercial terms, it does not use this data to train its models.

sections.heading: Service providers
paragraphs: We use a small number of providers to run Chatsoon. Except for Google as described below, they process personal information only on our instructions and only to provide their service to us:
bullets: Cloudflare, Inc.: hosts our servers, database and file storage (including profile and card photos), serves the website, and provides Turnstile bot protection for the Connect form.
Anthropic, PBC: reads card and badge photos when you use card scanning.
Resend: sends Chatsoon's emails, such as your sign-in codes and connect notifications.

Google LLC (Android app only): the QR code scanner uses Google ML Kit, which sends Google basic device and app information, performance metrics, error codes and a per-installation identifier to measure and improve the scanner. The iPhone app doesn't use ML Kit.

sections.heading: Sharing and international transfers
paragraphs: We don't share your personal information with anyone except the providers above, the people you choose to share with (for example through your public profile or a connection), and where the law requires it or it is needed to protect the rights, safety or property of our users, the public or Moshi Concepts Inc.
Our providers may process information in the United States and other countries. Where the law requires it, we use appropriate safeguards for these transfers.
Apple and Google run the app stores you download Chatsoon from and handle any information they collect under their own privacy policies.

sections.heading: Retention and deletion
bullets: We keep your information for as long as your account is open.

You can delete your account at any time: open the Me tab in the app, or sign in at https://chatsoon.app and open the Me tab, then tap Delete account. Your public profile link stops working straight away, and 24 hours later we permanently delete your account, profile, contacts, notes, tags, connections and the files you uploaded, including profile and card photos and the link preview images made from your profile. We email you a link to cancel during those 24 hours, and a final email once it's done. You can also email hello@chatsoon.app from the address you sign in with and we will delete it within 30 days.
Our database provider keeps backups for disaster recovery. Deleted data rolls off these backups automatically, within 30 days.
Reports you made, reports made about you and your blocks are deleted with your account. Copies of reports already sent to our moderation inbox may be kept until we finish reviewing them.

Contacts that other people saved about you, for example from your public profile or a connection, belong to their accounts and are not removed when you delete yours. You can ask them to remove it, or email us.
Technical logs are kept for a short time, no more than 30 days, unless we need them longer to investigate abuse or a security issue.

sections.heading: Export your data
paragraphs: You can download all your contacts as a CSV file at any time: open the Me tab in the app and tap Export contacts (CSV). You can open it in Excel, Google Sheets or Numbers, or import it into another tool.

sections.heading: Your choices and rights
paragraphs: You can view, change, export and delete your information in the app at any time. Depending on where you live, you may also have the right to access, correct, delete or move your personal information, and to object to or limit how we use it. To make a request, email hello@chatsoon.app from the address you sign in with. We'll respond within 30 days. You can also complain to your local data protection authority.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: Every connection to Chatsoon is encrypted with HTTPS, and our hosting provider encrypts stored data. Sign-in uses one-time codes instead of passwords. Photos are stored privately and can only be opened through short-lived signed links. Every request for private data is checked against your account, so no one else can see your contacts, notes or tags.
No system is perfectly secure. If you find a security problem, please tell us at hello@chatsoon.app.

sections.heading: Age requirement
paragraphs: Chatsoon is for adults. You must be 18 or older to use it. We don't knowingly collect information from anyone under 18. If you believe someone under 18 has given us their information, email hello@chatsoon.app and we'll delete it.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We'll update this page when our practices change and change the date at the top. If a change is significant, we'll let you know in the app or by email before it takes effect.

sections.heading: Contact us
paragraphs: Moshi Concepts Inc. Email hello@chatsoon.app with any question about privacy or your data.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: These Terms of Use ("Terms") are an agreement between you and Moshi Concepts Inc. ("we", "us") and apply to your use of Chatsoon, including the iOS and Android apps and chatsoon.app. By creating an account or using Chatsoon, you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy. If you don't agree, please don't use Chatsoon.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: You must be at least 18 years old and able to enter into a binding agreement to use Chatsoon. By using it, you confirm that you are. You may not use Chatsoon if we have previously removed you from the service.

sections.heading: Your account
paragraphs: You sign in with a one-time code sent to your email address. Keep your email account secure, because you are responsible for what happens on your Chatsoon account. Never share your sign-in code with anyone. If you think someone else has used your account, email hello@chatsoon.app.
Give accurate information about yourself. Don't create an account for someone else or pretend to be someone you're not.

sections.heading: Your content
paragraphs: You own the content you add to Chatsoon, including your profile, contacts, notes, tags and photos ("your content"). You give us a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to host, store, process, display and transmit your content only as needed to run Chatsoon for you, for example to show your public profile to the people you share it with, and to search engines if you turn that on, or to read a card photo when you ask us to. This licence ends when you delete the content or your account, apart from backups that roll off automatically.

You are responsible for your content and must have the right to add it. When you save details about other people, you are responsible for having a lawful reason to keep them and for using them respectfully and in line with the privacy laws that apply to you.

Your public profile can be seen by anyone who has its link or scans your QR code, and anyone searching the web if you turn on search visibility, so don't put anything on it that you want to keep private.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
paragraphs: You agree not to use Chatsoon to:
bullets: post or send content that is illegal, hateful, discriminatory, harassing, threatening, sexually explicit, violent, defamatory or otherwise objectionable;
harass, bully, stalk, threaten, intimidate or abuse anyone;
impersonate any person or organisation, or misrepresent who you are or who you work for;
send spam, scams, phishing or unsolicited bulk messages, including through the Connect form;
collect other people's information without their permission, or scrape, crawl or harvest data from Chatsoon;
infringe anyone's intellectual property, privacy or other rights;
upload malware, or try to break, overload, probe or get around the security of Chatsoon;
break any law, or help anyone else do any of these things.

sections.heading: Zero tolerance for objectionable content and abusive users
paragraphs: Chatsoon has zero tolerance for objectionable content and abusive users. Content or behaviour that breaks the acceptable use rules above is not allowed anywhere in Chatsoon, including on public profiles, in Connect form messages and in anything else you share with other people.

When we find, or are told about, content or behaviour that breaks these rules, we remove the content and eject the user responsible from Chatsoon, without notice. We may report serious cases to the authorities.

sections.heading: Reporting and blocking
bullets: Report: every public profile, every connection and every Connect form message has a Report option. Choose a reason, add details if you like and send it. You don't need an account to report a public profile on the web.

Block: when you're signed in, you can block anyone from their public profile or, if you're connected, from their contact page. Blocking removes them from your contacts and stops them from connecting with you in the app.
Connect form messages come from people who don't have a Chatsoon account, so they can't be blocked. Delete any you don't want, and report abusive ones.
We review every report within 24 hours. When content or a user breaks these Terms, we remove the content and eject the user.
You can also report a problem by emailing hello@chatsoon.app.

sections.heading: Card scanning
paragraphs: Card scanning uses AI to read the text in your photo. It can make mistakes, so check the details before you save them.

sections.heading: The service
paragraphs: We work hard to keep Chatsoon available and useful, but we may change, add or remove features, and the service may sometimes be unavailable. Chatsoon is free to use today. If we ever introduce paid features, we'll tell you first and you won't be charged unless you choose to pay.

sections.heading: Our intellectual property
paragraphs: Chatsoon, including its name, logo, design and software, belongs to Moshi Concepts Inc. We give you a personal, non-transferable, revocable licence to use the apps and website as they are intended to be used. You may not copy, modify, reverse engineer, sell or resell any part of Chatsoon, except where the law allows it.

sections.heading: Termination
paragraphs: You can stop using Chatsoon and delete your account at any time: open the Me tab in the app, or sign in at https://chatsoon.app and open the Me tab, then tap Delete account. You can also email hello@chatsoon.app and ask us to delete it.

We may suspend or end your account, or remove your content, at any time if you break these Terms, if the law requires it, or if we need to protect our users or Chatsoon. The sections of these Terms that by their nature should continue after your account ends, including the disclaimers and limitation of liability, will continue to apply.

sections.heading: Disclaimers
paragraphs: Chatsoon is provided "as is" and "as available". To the fullest extent the law allows, we make no warranties of any kind, express or implied, including warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement. We don't promise that Chatsoon will be uninterrupted, error free or secure, or that information from other users, the Connect form or card scanning is accurate.
You are responsible for your dealings with the people you meet through Chatsoon.

sections.heading: Limitation of liability
paragraphs: To the fullest extent the law allows, Moshi Concepts Inc. and its directors, employees and suppliers will not be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for any loss of data, profits, revenue, goodwill or business opportunities, arising out of or related to your use of Chatsoon. Some places don't allow these limits, so they apply to you only as far as the law allows. Nothing in these Terms limits any rights you have under consumer protection laws that cannot be excluded.

sections.heading: App stores
paragraphs: If you downloaded Chatsoon from the Apple App Store, you also agree that these Terms are between you and Moshi Concepts Inc., not Apple; that Apple has no obligation to provide maintenance or support for Chatsoon; that Apple is not responsible for any claims about Chatsoon, including product liability claims, claims that it fails to meet legal requirements, and claims that it infringes someone else's intellectual property; and that Apple and its subsidiaries are third-party beneficiaries of these Terms and may enforce them against you.
Your use of Chatsoon must also follow the terms of the app store you downloaded it from.

sections.heading: Changes to these Terms
paragraphs: We may update these Terms from time to time. We'll post the new version on this page and change the date at the top, and we'll let you know in the app or by email about significant changes. If you keep using Chatsoon after the changes take effect, you accept the updated Terms.

sections.heading: General
paragraphs: These Terms and our Privacy Policy are the whole agreement between you and us about Chatsoon. If any part of these Terms can't be enforced, the rest still applies. If we don't enforce a right, we haven't given it up. You may not transfer your rights under these Terms. We may transfer ours as part of a merger, acquisition or sale of assets.

sections.heading: Contact us
paragraphs: Questions about these Terms? Email hello@chatsoon.app.

support.title: Support
support.intro: Need a hand with Chatsoon? Start with the answers below. If you can't find what you need, email hello@chatsoon.app and we'll get back to you. We usually reply within one business day.

sections.heading: Getting started
paragraphs: Open Chatsoon, enter your email address and type in the 6 digit code we send you. There's no password to remember. Then add your name to create your profile. You can add a photo, headline, company, role and links at any time.

sections.heading: How do I connect with someone?
bullets: You both have Chatsoon: open the My QR tab and let them scan it from the app, or tap Scan someone to scan theirs. You both get each other's card straight away.

They don't have the app: they can scan your QR code with their phone's camera. It opens your public profile at chatsoon.app, where they can save your contact card and send you their details with the Connect form. Their details land straight in your contacts.
Not in the same room: tap Share or Copy link on the My QR tab and send your profile link in any messaging app.

sections.heading: How do I scan a business card or badge?
paragraphs: Open the Add tab and tap Photograph a card or badge. Take a clear, well-lit photo of the business card or event badge. Chatsoon reads the details with AI and fills them in for you. Check them on the review screen, fix anything that's wrong, then save.

Tap Scan a QR code on the Add tab to scan QR codes from Telegram, LinkedIn or X, a digital business card (vCard) or a website link. Chatsoon turns them into a contact for you to review. Or tap Type it in to add someone by hand.

sections.heading: Does Chatsoon work offline?
paragraphs: Yes. At a busy venue with poor signal, you can still add contacts and take card photos. They're saved on your phone and sent automatically when you're back online. Card details are read once the photo has been sent, and your contact list refreshes when you reconnect.

sections.heading: How do tags, notes and priority work?
paragraphs: Open a contact to add tags such as Sponsor, Investor or Founder, write notes, set a priority from 1 (low) to 5 (top) and record the event where you met. You can create your own tags and delete the ones you don't need.
Search your contacts by name, company, tag or notes, or filter the list by tag. Tap a contact's links to message them on Telegram, email them, or open their LinkedIn or X profile.

sections.heading: How do I export my contacts?
paragraphs: Open the Me tab and tap Export contacts (CSV). Chatsoon creates a CSV file of all your contacts that you can open in Excel, Google Sheets or Numbers, or import into another tool.

sections.heading: How do I show or hide my profile on Google?
paragraphs: Open Edit profile, then Search engines, and turn Show my profile in search engines on or off. It's off by default. Your phone and messaging details are never shown to search engines. If you turn it off, removal from search engines usually takes a few days to a few weeks.

sections.heading: How do I delete some of my data without deleting my account?
paragraphs: Chatsoon is published by Moshi Concepts Inc. You can delete individual pieces of your data at any time, in the app or by signing in at https://chatsoon.app:
bullets: A contact: open it and tap Delete contact. This deletes the contact with its notes, tags and card photo.
A note: open the contact, clear the note and save.
Tags: open the Me tab, tap Manage tags and delete the tags you don't need.
Your profile photo: open the Me tab, tap Edit profile, then Remove photo.
Your headline, company, role, links, booking links, and phone, WhatsApp and Signal details: open the Me tab, tap Edit profile, clear what you want to delete and tap Save.
By email: email hello@chatsoon.app from the address you sign in with and tell us what to delete. We will delete it within 30 days.

Deleted data is removed from Chatsoon straight away. It rolls off our database provider's backups within 30 days, and technical logs are kept no more than 30 days. Contacts other people saved about you, for example from your public profile or a connection, stay in their accounts. To delete everything, delete your account (below).

sections.heading: How do I delete my account?
paragraphs: Chatsoon is published by Moshi Concepts Inc. You can delete your Chatsoon account in any of these ways, even if you no longer have the app installed:
bullets: In the app: open the Me tab, tap Delete account. You'll be offered the chance to export your contacts as a CSV first, then type DELETE to confirm. Your public profile goes offline straight away, and your account is permanently deleted 24 hours later. We email you a link to cancel during those 24 hours, and a final email once it's done.
Without the app: sign in at https://chatsoon.app with your email address, open the Me tab, tap Delete account and follow the same steps.
By email: email hello@chatsoon.app from the address you sign in with and ask us to delete your account. We will delete it within 30 days.

Deleting your account permanently deletes your account, profile, contacts, notes, tags, connections and photos, and it can't be undone. Your public profile link stops working immediately. Backups roll off within 30 days, technical logs are kept no more than 30 days, and copies of reports already sent to our moderation inbox may be kept until we finish reviewing them. Contacts other people saved about you stay in their accounts. If you want to keep your contacts, export them first.

sections.heading: How do I report or block someone?
paragraphs: In the app, open their profile, or their contact if you're connected, and tap Report or Block. On the web, use the Report profile link on any public profile. You don't need an account to report.
A message someone sent you with the Connect form on your public page comes from a person without an account. Open it in Contacts and tap Report, then delete it if you don't want it.
We review every report within 24 hours and remove content and users that break our Terms of Use.

sections.heading: I didn't get my sign-in code
paragraphs: Check your spam or junk folder, and make sure your email address is spelled correctly. Codes expire after 10 minutes, so request a new one if it's been longer. Still stuck? Email hello@chatsoon.app.

sections.heading: Contact us
paragraphs: Email hello@chatsoon.app with your question. If it's about your account, send it from the email address you sign in with so we can find your account. We will never ask for your sign-in code, so please don't share it with anyone.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: We want chatsoon.app and the Chatsoon web app to work for everyone, including people who use a screen reader, navigate by keyboard, zoom or resize text, or turn on reduced motion. This page explains what we've done, what we know still needs work, and how to tell us about a problem.

sections.heading: Our commitment
paragraphs: We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA for chatsoon.app (the public pages and your public profile) and for the signed-in Chatsoon web app. We test with automated tools and by using the app with a keyboard and a screen reader, and we keep working through anything we find.

sections.heading: What's supported
bullets: Keyboard: every screen, form and dialog can be used with Tab, Enter, Space and Escape alone, with a visible focus ring.
Screen readers: pages use headings, landmarks, labelled form fields and live regions for errors and status updates, and icon-only buttons carry a text label.
Light and dark mode: the app follows your device or browser's system setting automatically.
Text resizing and zoom: text can be resized or the page zoomed to 200% without losing content or function.
Reduced motion: if you've turned on "reduce motion" on your device or in your browser, Chatsoon's loading animations turn off.
Colour contrast: text and interactive elements meet WCAG AA contrast ratios.

sections.heading: Known limitations
paragraphs: We're not aware of any WCAG 2.2 AA failures on chatsoon.app or the web app today, but a few things are worth calling out:
bullets: Some screens group content into fewer landmark regions (such as "main" or "navigation") than we'd like, which can make jumping between sections by landmark slower with a screen reader, even though every control on the page is still reachable.

Scanning a QR code or a business card uses your camera and needs you to see and aim it. If that's not possible, ask the other person to share their profile link instead, or use "Add manually" to type in a contact's details.
Booking links (such as Calendly or Google Calendar) open that provider's own page, which follows its own accessibility standards, not ours.
We test with the latest versions of common screen readers and browsers. If you use an older or less common combination and something doesn't work, please tell us.

sections.heading: The iPhone and Android apps
paragraphs: The Chatsoon iPhone and Android apps share the same design, wording and navigation as the web app, and support your device's screen reader (VoiceOver or TalkBack), Dynamic Type or font scaling, and system light and dark mode. We improve their accessibility in every release, using the same testing we do for the web app.

sections.heading: How to report a problem
paragraphs: If you hit an accessibility barrier anywhere in Chatsoon, on the web or in the app, email hello@chatsoon.app with the page or screen, what happened, and the assistive technology or browser you were using. We'll respond within 5 business days.
